heading: 4.1.1 Matrix Confidence Assessment
text: Scores biological plausibility enriched metabolite set within specified biological sample matrix.Input: Biological matrix type (e.g., "urine", "plasma", "serum", "blood", "feces")Output: Per-metabolite-set matrix confidence score (0–100) reflecting whether metabolite set represents coherent biologically plausible biochemical entity within specified sample matrix

heading: 4.1.2 Topic Relevance Assessment
text: Searches PubMed scores enriched metabolite set based published evidence linking specific research context.Input: Research topic (e.g., "type 2 diabetes", "colorectal cancer", "pregnancy")Output: Per-metabolite-set topic relevance score supporting PubMed literature (PMIDs)

heading: 6 Installation
text: featureMSEA implements Feature-Based Metabolite Set Enrichment Analysis — method performs functional interpretation directly ranked mass spectrometry features, without requiring complete metabolite identification arbitrary significance threshold preselect features.Install TidyMass dependencies first, featureMSEA package GitHub:installed, load required packages start session:
code:
# Install TidyMass dependencies first
remotes::install_gitlab("tidymass/masstools")
remotes::install_gitlab("tidymass/massdataset")
remotes::install_gitlab("tidymass/metid")

# Install featuremsea
remotes::install_github("tidymass/featuremsea")
library(masstools)
library(massdataset)
library(metid)
library(featuremsea)

heading: 7.1 Required inputs
text: primary input featureMSEA feature table — data frame row represents one LC-MS feature. following columns required:analysis additionally requires two reference databases:MS1 metabolite database — accurate-mass-based feature annotation (m/z matching). Supported: KEGG, HMDB.Metabolite set database — defines sets metabolites tested enrichment. Supported: KEGG, SMPDB, IMETPD, Reactome, WikiPathways.databases can downloaded TidyMass website.

heading: 7.2 Demo data
text: ready--use demo feature table available download:Feature table: Demo dataMS1 database Metabolite set databases: Download hereLoad feature table databases R session proceeding annotation step:

# Load feature table (if saved as .rda)
load("feature_table.rda")        # loads object: feature_table

# Load MS1 metabolite database (example: KEGG compound MS1 database)

# Load metabolite set database (example: KEGG pathway database)

heading: 8.1 Step 2 — Annotate feature table
text: Features annotated MS1 database via accurate mass matching. Co-eluting features similar retention times grouped Metabolic Feature Clusters (MFCs) improve annotation confidence reduce redundancy.Key parameters:Tip: Use "rp" lipidomics general metabolomics experiments. Switch "hilic" polar metabolite profiling.
code:
annotation_table_final <-
  annotate_feature_table(
    feature_table       = feature_table,
    column              = "rp",
    metabolite_database = kegg_compound_ms1, # use downloaded MS1 database
    database_type       = "KEGG",            # "KEGG" or "HMDB"
    ms1_match_ppm       = 15,
    mfc_rt_tol          = 10,
    isotope_number      = 3
  )

heading: 8.2 Step 3 — Remove redundant annotations
text: initial annotation, redundant entries arising isotopes, adducts, -source fragments removed. cleaned annotation table processed produce ranking table annotation table used enrichment analysis.two output objects feed directly enrichment step:ranking_table — links feature ranking statistic used enrichment scoring.annotation_table — links features candidate metabolite annotations.
code:
annotation_table_final2 <-
  featuremsea::remove_redundancy(
    annotation_table = annotation_table_final
  )

results <- process_annotation_table(
  annotation_table_final2 = annotation_table_final2,
  database_type            = "KEGG"   # "KEGG" or "HMDB"
)

ranking_table    <- results$ranking_table
annotation_table <- results$original_score_annotation

heading: 9.1 Step 4 — Run enrichment analysis
text: perform_fmsea_analysis() ranks features condition statistic, computes running enrichment score metabolite set, estimates significance via permutation testing. Results returned fmsea S4 object.
code:
# Supported metabolite set databases: KEGG, SMPDB, IMETPD, Reactome, Wikipathway
fmsea_result <- perform_fmsea_analysis(
  pathway_database,           # metabolite set database object (from Step 1)
  annotation_table,           # from process_annotation_table() in Step 3
  ranking_table,              # from process_annotation_table() in Step 3
  threads          = 6,
  min.compounds.num = 15,
  max.compounds.num = 300,
  id.col           = "KEGG_ID",
  perm.num         = 10000,
  seed             = 123,
  fdr.thr          = 0.05,
  max.iter.num     = 3,
  verbose          = TRUE
)

# Significant pathways are stored in:
fmsea_result@significant_modules

heading: 9.2 Parameters
text: Note: Increasing perm.num improves p-value precision increases runtime proportionally. 1000 permutations gives good balance exploratory analysis; use 10,000+ publication-quality results.

heading: 10.1 Step 5 — Optional LLM evaluation
text: Two optional functions use Large Language Models (LLMs) evaluate biological plausibility enriched metabolite sets. require API key supported provider.API provider choice: functions require explicit provider selection — either "openai" "siliconflow". Default models: gpt-4.1 / Qwen/Qwen3-32B (chat); text-embedding-3-small / Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B (embedding). Custom models can specified via model argument.

heading: 10.2 Step 5a — Matrix confidence assessment
text: Assesses reliably metabolites sample matrix (urine, plasma, etc.) expected indicate pathway’s activity.following columns added fmsea_result@significant_modules:
code:
# Using OpenAI
fmsea_result <- analyze_matrix_relevance(
  fmsea_result,
  sample_source = "urine",         # biological matrix of your sample
  api_key       = "sk-openai-xxx", # OpenAI API key
  provider      = "openai"
)

# Using SiliconFlow / Qwen (recommended for users in China)
fmsea_result <- analyze_matrix_relevance(
  results       = fmsea_result,
  sample_source = "plasma",
  api_key       = "sk-siliconflow-xxx",
  provider      = "siliconflow"
)

heading: 10.3 Step 5b — Topic relevance assessment
text: Links significant pathways research topic using PubMed literature search embedding-based re-ranking.following columns added fmsea_result@significant_modules:Caution: LLM outputs probabilistic. Always verify AI-generated interpretations primary literature. Use module guide hypothesis generation, replace domain expertise.
code:
fmsea_result <- analyze_topic_relevance(
  results           = fmsea_result,
  research_topic    = "type 2 diabetes",
  api_key           = "sk-siliconflow-xxx",
  provider          = "siliconflow",
  pubmed_api_key    = NULL,   # optional; increases PubMed rate limit
  similarity_cutoff = 0.6     # cosine similarity threshold for fuzzy matches
)

heading: 11.1 Step 6 — Plot enrichment results
text: plot_fmsea_plot() generates multi-panel enrichment plot single pathway interest.plot includes four panels:Enrichment score curve — running enrichment score across ranked feature list, peak marking leading-edge boundary.Ranked feature hits — vertical bars showing features annotated pathway metabolites fall ranked list.Annotation weights — per-feature annotation confidence scores.Pair weights — feature–metabolite pair weights used enrichment scoring.find valid pathway_id values, inspect significant modules table:
code:
# Plot enrichment results for a specific pathway
plot_fmsea_plot(
  fmsea_obj  = fmsea_result,
  pathway_id = "hsa00010",                  # pathway ID from significant_modules

# View significant pathways and their IDs
head(fmsea_result@significant_modules)
